blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Single-photon lidar records the arrival time of each returning photon, enabling 3D reconstruction from few views and scarce photons. However, leading neural methods such as Transientangelo require over an hour of non-convex per-scene optimization, and their accuracy degrades as photon flux decreases. We propose FirstCross, a network-free approach that instead solves a short sequence of convex problems on a voxel grid. For a solid object, the Poisson likelihood of a ray with given signal and background rates depends on the scene solely through its first crossing, the point where the ray first enters the object. Decomposing this likelihood yields two tractable terms. The first penalizes surfaces in front of detected photons and admits a tight convex closure, namely volume rendering with a running-maximum transmittance in place of NeRF's product transmittance. The second accounts for photons that no surface explains and admits a convex upper bound once the object is assumed to be thick behind each detected surface point. Compared with Transientangelo under its own real-data protocol, FirstCross achieves lower depth error across every test scene, view count, and flux level. With three views and 100 times fewer photons than at the protocol's lowest flux, our mean object depth error stays under half of Transientangelo's with all photons. Given our detected surface points, the best classical fusion has 1.3 to 1.8 times our three-view error across flux levels. On real room-scale captures with 1% of their photons, TransientNeRF has 2.8 to 7.7 times our error. FirstCross lets few-view single-photon scanners cut exposure to 1% and reconstruct an object in about a minute on one GPU.
blocks.zh: 单光子 lidar 记录每个返回光子的到达时间, 使得 3D 重建 从很少的视图和稀缺的光子。 然而,如Tranientangelo等主要神经方法需要超过一个小时的非锥形每层优化,其精度随着光子通量的减少而下降. 我们提出FirstCross,一种无网络的方法,代替解决一个voxel网格上的短序对流问题. 对于一个固体物体来说,带有给定信号和背景速率的射线的普瓦松概率,仅取决于场景通过其第一次穿越,即射线首先进入物体的点. 分解这种可能性会产生两个可拉动术语. 第一类惩罚在检测到的光子前表面,并承认收紧的对流闭合,即用最大流速的体积渲染来代替NERF的产品传播. 第二个是光子,没有表面解释,一旦假定物体在每一个探测到的表面点后面有厚度,就会承认一个对流上方的束缚. 与Transientangelo在自己的真数据协议下相比,FirstCross在每一个测试场景中实现较低的深度误差,视图计数,和通量水平. 与协议的最低通量相比,我们的平均物体深度误差 低于Transientangelo所有光子的一半 根据我们检测到的表面点, 最好的古典聚变 有1.3到1.8倍 我们的三视误差 跨通量水平。 在真实的室量级捕捉 以1%的光子, TransientNERF 有2.8到7.7倍 我们的错误。 FirstCross允许少数查看单光子扫描仪将曝光率削减到1%,并在约一分钟后在一个GPU上重建一个对象.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: In single-photon lidar, a pulsed laser and a single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) record a transient histogram of photon arrival times at each pixel. Each signal photon measures range, and a few of them locate a surface to within the width of the instrument response function (IRF), the timing jitter of laser and detector. However, fast acquisition, long range or low-power sensors yield fewer than one photon per pixel [ 11 , 38 ] , as at 0.1 photons per occupied pixel (PPP) in Fig. 1 .

blocks.en: Prior work follows two main routes. The classical route detects a return on each ray (the arrival time of the echo from the surface) and fuses the returns [ 8 ] and the free space in front of them [ 4 , 49 ] across views. A ray without a return contributes nothing, although the absence of photons is evidence of free space. The strongest neural methods, transient neural radiance fields [ 23 , 24 ] and their surface variant Transientangelo [ 22 ] , instead volume-render histograms from a neural field and fit the measurements bin by bin. They are accurate with many photons, but fitting each scene takes over an hour and the objective is non-convex.
blocks.zh: 前期工程主要走两条路线. 古典路线探测每个射线上的返回(从表面回声的到达时间),并将返回 [8] 和它们面前的自由空间[4,49] 对视线进行引信. 虽然光子的缺乏是自由空间的证据,但是没有返回的射线却无济于事。 最强的神经方法,瞬态神经辐射场[23,24]及其表面变体Transientangelo[22],转而将神经场的体积直径图进行回转,并按本位进行测量. 它们与许多光子是准确的,但每个场景的安装需要1个多小时,目标为非凸轮.

blocks.en:
We propose FirstCross, which starts instead from the photon likelihood ( Fig. 2 ). Our key observation is that, for a solid object, photon arrivals along a ray with given signal and background rates depend on the scene only through one point: the first intersection of the ray with the object, which we call the first crossing . We write the Poisson likelihood of every ray, with or without photons, as a function of its first crossing and then of the occupancies of its samples in an implicit field on a voxel grid.
This likelihood is combinatorial in the occupancies, but it splits into two parts. The too-early part, where a surface blocks the path of a photon, is submodular in the set of occupied samples. Its tight convex closure, the largest convex function that matches it on binary occupancies, has a closed form: volume rendering whose transmittance is one minus the running maximum of occupancy along the ray, in place of NeRF’s product transmittance. The too-late part, where no surface explains a photon, is supermodular and the only source of non-convexity. It requires the ray to enter the object before the photon arrives without specifying where. Our thickness assumption , that objects are thicker than a few IRF widths, supplies the location, because the point just behind a detected return then lies inside the object. Each solver iteration therefore works on a convex problem, and the minimum of the first problem does not depend on the initial grid, although our solver reaches it only approximately. With the product transmittance, by contrast, an optimisation started from an occupied grid can leave free space filled. We make three contributions: • We show that the first-crossing Poisson likelihood splits into a submodular too-early part and a supermodular too-late part. We derive the tight convex closure of the too-early part in closed form, which is volume rendering with a running-maximum transmittance. • We derive a convex upper bound on the too-late part from the thickness assumption. Our solver needs no neural network and reconstructs an object in about a minute. • We demonstrate lower depth error than Transientangelo on every test scene, view count and flux level of its own real-capture protocol. From three views, our error on the object stays below Transientangelo’s at full flux even with inputs thinned 100-fold below its lowest flux of 10 PPP. Scope. We assume solid objects, known camera poses and negligible pile-up, which biases detections toward early time bins at high flux. Thin sheets, partially transmissive layers [ 45 ] and mixed pixels at silhouettes are not modelled.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Neural transient fields. TransientNeRF [ 23 ] introduced volume rendering of multi-view transient histograms. Transientangelo [ 22 ] then targeted sparse views and low flux with a neural signed distance field [ 17 ] and regularisers. Other work models propagating light [ 24 , 25 ] , outdoor scenes [ 37 ] , low-cost sensors [ 29 ] and mixed returns [ 45 ] , or learns to reconstruct from a single transient [ 16 ] , and SP-TransientBench [ 5 ] provides room-scale captures.
blocks.zh: 神经瞬间球场. TransientNERF [23]引入了多视图瞬间直径图的体积渲染. Transientangelo[22]然后用神经标志的距离场[17]和常态器瞄准稀疏的视线和低通量. 其他工作模式宣传光[24,25],户外场景[37],低成本传感器[29]和混合回报[45],或学习从单一瞬间重建[16],SP-Transition Bench[5]提供房间尺度的捕捉.

blocks.en: Photon-efficient depth imaging. First-photon imaging [ 11 ] and later work [ 38 , 34 , 6 , 19 , 32 , 40 ] use Poisson statistics for single-view depth, with spatial priors over neighbouring pixels. With several views, all first crossings lie on one surface, so our field couples rays across views.
blocks.zh: 光子高效深度成像. 初光成像[11],后作[38,34,6,19,32,40] 使用普瓦逊统计法进行单视深度,空间前兆大于相邻像素. 有几种观点,所有第一次穿越都位于一个表面,所以我们的野外情侣横跨了各种观点.

blocks.en: Range fusion and implicit surfaces. Volumetric fusion [ 4 ] and its robust convex forms [ 49 ] combine per-ray distances. Poisson-type reconstruction [ 9 , 8 , 2 , 33 ] and radial basis functions [ 3 ] fit an implicit function to oriented points, and variants estimate orientation [ 18 , 7 ] or add visibility envelopes [ 10 ] . Our bending prior follows [ 2 , 3 ] , but our data term lets zero-photon rays carve free space and weights rays by effective photon counts.
blocks.zh: 范围聚变和隐含表面. 卷体聚变[4]及其坚固的对流形成[49]结合了每射线距离. Poisson-type重建[9,8,2,33]和射线基础函数[3]将一个隐含的函数适合方向点,变体估计方向[18,7]或添加能见度信封[10]. 我们之前的弯曲跟随着[2,3],但我们的数据术语允许零光子射线通过有效的光子计数来刻出自由空间和权重射线.

blocks.en: Visibility in surface reconstruction. Space carving [ 13 ] and continuous multi-view stereo [ 12 ] use per-voxel photo-consistency, and s s – t t cuts [ 14 ] and VASE [ 41 ] use soft free-space constraints from points. Closest to ours are ray potentials [ 20 , 35 , 42 ] , whose cost depends on a ray’s first occupied voxel and is minimised discretely or by a convex relaxation with a non-convex visibility constraint [ 36 ] . Concurrently, Lenain et al . [ 15 ] regress the first intersection of a 1-Lipschitz network, a non-convex problem. We share this first-crossing structure and submodular tools [ 21 , 1 , 30 ] , but our cost is the photon likelihood, and we derive the tight convex closure of its too-early part and a convex bound on its too-late part. This closure is a running-maximum rendering that models visibility in a convex functional.
blocks.zh: 表面重建的可见度. 空间刻 [13] 和连续多视图立体 [12] 使用每伏xel摄影一致性,s – t 切 [14] 和 VASE [41] 使用来自点的软自由空间限制. 离我们最近的是射线潜力[20,35,42],其成本取决于射线第一个占用的阴道,并且被离散地或通过有非视线可见性限制的对流放松来最小化[36]. 同时,Lenain et al. [15] 倒退了1-Lipschitz网络的第一个交叉点,这是一个非汇流问题. 我们分享了这种第一次交叉的结构和亚模块工具[21, 1, 30],但我们的成本是光子可能性,我们得出了它太早部分的紧密对流关闭,以及它太晚部分的对流束缚. 这种关闭是一种运行的最大渲染,使模型在对流功能中的能见度.

blocks.en: Volume rendering of surfaces. NeRF [ 26 ] composites independent opacities. NeuS [ 44 ] , VolSDF [ 47 ] and UNISURF [ 31 ] derive them from an implicit surface but keep the product along the ray. NeuS matches the running maximum on rays that cross one surface. IDR [ 46 ] renders the first intersection alone, and non-exponential transmittance [ 43 , 39 ] and stochastic geometry [ 27 ] model opaque surfaces. All of these agree on binary occupancy and differ on fractional values. The running maximum is convex, and Proposition 1 shows that no convex extension is tighter.
blocks.zh: 表面的体积渲染. NERF[26]复合材料独立不透明. NeuS [44], VolSDF [47] 和 UNISURF [31] 从一个隐含的表面得到它们,但将产品保留在射线上. NeuS与跨越一个表面的射线上的运行极限匹配. IDR [46] 使第一个交叉点单独存在,非主动传递 [43,39] 和结构几何 [27] 模型不透明表面. 所有这些都同意二进制占用,并在分数值上存在差异. 运行中的最大值是凸轮,Proposition 1显示没有凸轮扩展更紧.

blocks.en: 3 From Photons to a Convex Functional
blocks.zh: 3 从光子到凸轮函数

blocks.en: From a few transient histograms with known poses, we seek a field u u on a voxel grid that is positive exactly inside the object. We write the likelihood of a ray through its first crossing, replace its too-early and too-late parts with convex surrogates, and minimise the resulting functional ( Fig. 2 ). Sec. S1 gives proofs and derivations.
blocks.zh: 从几个有已知姿势的瞬态直方图中,我们寻找一个场u u 在一个正方形物体内部的voxel网格上。 我们写出射线穿过其第一次穿越的可能性,用对流代位取代其太早和太晚的部分,并尽量减少由此产生的功能(图2)。 S1法官提供了证据和推论。

The closure follows from the Lovász extension formula [ 21 , 1 ] , which averages the set function over the level sets of the occupancies. 3.6 Return Detection
blocks.zh: 3.6 返回检测

blocks.en: The statistics in the functional are computed from the histograms with standard detection steps (Sec. S2). On objects, each ray pools the photons of 4 × 4 4\times 4 pixels (one pixel on rooms), while depth is still rendered at every pixel. We take the return t ^ r \hat{t}_{r} of a ray as the centroid of its earliest strong matched-filter response, and a ray has a return if its local false-discovery rate against simulated background-only rays is at most 1 / 2 1/2 , with no threshold tuned per scene or flux. Rays without a return are treated as zero-photon rays. The full-flux captures are provided with object masks applied, and at low flux we use the masks of Transientangelo, giving both methods identical inputs.

blocks.en: To minimise E E , we alternate a dual update along rays with a linear solve for u u . The dual update writes each running maximum as a maximum over distributions of where the ray enters the object and gives each sample a weight W W . With these weights fixed, we replace each term by a quadratic model (Alg. S1). We run 12 iterations from the empty grid u = − β ​ ε u=-\beta\varepsilon with unit slope and cosine. Each iteration is one damped dual update and one solve by FFT-preconditioned conjugate gradients, after which the slopes, cosines, scales and witnesses are updated. blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en: Datasets and protocol. We follow the protocol of Transientangelo [ 22 ] : its real captures, two, three or five input views, ten novel views, full flux and its low-flux settings of 300 to 10 PPP. Transientangelo results are obtained from its released checkpoints, which reproduce 14 of its 16 published three-view results (Sec. S3). We further simulate 1 and 0.1 PPP, and down to 0.003 PPP in Fig. 4 , by binomial thinning of 10 PPP, which keeps its signal-to-background ratio. The official depth error averages | d ^ − d | |\hat{d}-d| over the frame, with zero outside the ground-truth mask. On baskets and food, this mask includes the turntable’s back wall. We therefore also report the object depth MAE, which further zeroes the error beyond 0.30 m from the scene origin. For room scale, we use the real rooms of SP-TransientBench [ 5 ] at full flux and thinned to 1%. All parameters are set on the validation scenes cinema, carving and library_floor2. We report single runs, and Sec. S5 adds repeated runs, other thinnings, extra ambient photons and camera rotations.

blocks.en: Comparison to Transientangelo. Table 1 and Tab. S4 show that ours has the lower official depth error on every test scene and flux level of the protocol with two, three and five views. With three views, our mean error is 2.97 mm at both full flux and 10 PPP, whereas Transientangelo’s rises from 4.70 to 7.04 mm. This is a reduction of 37% and 58%, respectively, and Sec. S2 gives bootstrap intervals. Our return detection accounts for much of the gap: TV-L1 fusion [ 49 ] of our detected returns has less than half the object depth MAE of Transientangelo at full flux and 10 PPP ( Tabs. 1 and 2 ). However, the best classical fusion has 1.3 to 1.8 times our mean object depth MAE at every flux level in Tab. S6. On an RTX 4090, ours takes 51 s in total on chef at 10 PPP, and Transientangelo trains for 1 h 26 min.

blocks.en: In Fig. 5 and Tab. S8, the two methods differ most in holes and floaters, which dominate the mean error, but their medians are close at full flux. At 10 PPP, Transientangelo’s median grows 2.7 and 5.4 times on chef and baskets, while ours changes by at most 7%. Down to 1 PPP, three orders of magnitude below full flux, our object depth MAE grows by at most 19% on any three-view scene (Tab. S3). Our Chamfer distance is lower on every three-view test scene and protocol flux level, but Transientangelo has better completeness and F-score at 2 mm in most of them (Sec. S4).

blocks.en: Lower photon counts. In Fig. 4 and Tab. S6, our mean object depth MAE stays below Transientangelo’s at full flux, and below TV-L1 fusion and screened Poisson reconstruction [ 8 ] of our detected returns, down to fewer than 10 3 10^{3} photons in three views. At the lowest flux, the reconstruction extends beyond the object, which the object depth MAE ignores (Sec. S5). Without masks, our object depth MAE at 0.01 PPP is 2.04 mm, against 1.94 mm with masks and 9.39 mm for the visual hull of the masks alone. Retrained with its official configuration, Transientangelo has a depth error of 5.48 mm on chef at 10 PPP, close to the 5.17 mm of its released checkpoint in Tab. 1 . At 1 PPP, however, it recovers no surface with or without adapted settings (Sec. S3), whereas ours has 1.08 mm. With its photons pooled as in ours, the adapted Transientangelo recovers chef and baskets at 1 PPP with 7.6 and 1.9 times our depth error.

blocks.en: Ablation study. Table 2 compares our variants with TV-L1 fusion [ 49 ] , the most accurate of three classical fusions down to 0.03 PPP (Tab. S6). Compared with NeRF’s product transmittance [ 26 ] , the closure helps most at low flux, without masks and when the solver starts from an occupied grid. Even the single convex problem cuts the product variant’s error at 0.1 PPP from 3.02 to 1.35 mm and removes most of its floaters ( Fig. 6 ). From an empty grid, this problem has a lower object depth MAE than Transientangelo on every three-view test scene and protocol flux level (Tab. S15), and ours improves on it most at 0.1 PPP.
blocks.zh: 校勘研究. 表2比较了我们的变体与TV-L1聚变[49],这是三个古典聚变中最准确的,下降到0.03 PPP(Tab. S6). 与NERF的产品传输[26]相比,关闭在低通量,没有口罩以及解答器从被占用的网格开始时最有帮助. 即使单对流问题也将产品变体的误差从3.02毫米降至1.35毫米,并移除其大部分浮体(图6 ). 从空网格来看,这个问题在每一个三景测试场景和协议通量水平(Tab. S15)上,对象深度MAE比Transientangelo低,我们的改进最多为0.1PP.

blocks.en: Without masks, the product variant produces spurious surfaces in front of the cameras ( Tabs. 2 and 6 , Fig. S13), with 2.5 to 7.3 times our error at 0.01 PPP (Tab. S15). From the occupied grid u = 0 u=0 , it leaves free space filled even with masks, whereas down to 0.1 PPP this start changes the single convex problem’s error by at most 0.17 mm, due to inexact convergence. With L-BFGS from an empty grid, with or without masks, the product comes within 12% of the closure’s mean error. From the occupied grid u = β ​ ε u=\beta\varepsilon , however, the product under L-BFGS fills free space without masks at 0.01 PPP on three of four scenes, unlike the closure (Tab. S16, Fig. S15). Without the too-early term, the error averages 4.6 to 40 times ours down to 0.1 PPP on validation and test scenes, and without the too-late term, holes open where photons are few. When q q , τ \tau or α \alpha is halved or doubled, the mean object depth MAE on the validation objects changes by at most 2%, and for ω \omega or β \beta , by at most 9% (Tab. S12).

blocks.en: Room scale. Across all rooms and view counts in Tab. 3 , with unchanged dimensionless parameters, ours is 2.8 to 7.7 times more accurate than TransientNeRF at 1% flux ( Fig. 7 ) and less accurate at full flux. We do not run Transientangelo on rooms, as its configuration assumes a bounding sphere of radius 0.4 m and object masks at low flux. Ours takes 3 min on library_floor2, whereas TransientNeRF trains for 10 to 17 h. blocks.en: We presented FirstCross, which reconstructs solid objects from a few views of single-photon lidar when photons are scarce. For a solid object, the Poisson likelihood of a ray with given signal and background rates is a function of its first crossing alone. Its too-early part has a tight convex closure, volume rendering with a running maximum, as does the non-increasing part of any first-crossing cost. Its too-late part has a convex upper bound under the thickness assumption. FirstCross therefore works through a short sequence of convex problems without a neural network, in about a minute per object. It has lower depth error than Transientangelo [ 22 ] in every setting of the original real-capture protocol. With three-view inputs thinned 100-fold below the protocol’s lowest flux, its mean object depth MAE stays under half of Transientangelo’s at full flux. FirstCross suits few-view 3D scanning of objects and rooms when acquisition must be fast. Code will be released.

FirstCross因此在没有神经网络的情况下,通过短序的对流问题工作,每物体约1分钟. 它的深度误差低于Transientangelo [22] 在原始真实捕捉协议的每一个设置中. 由于三视输入在协议最低通量下100倍稀释,其平均物体深度MAE保持在Transientangelo全通量的一半以下。 FirstCross suits 少见 3D 扫描对象和房间 当获取必须快。 代码将被发布。

blocks.en: Limitations and Future Work. The thickness assumption requires objects thicker than the band ε \varepsilon , about 24 cm at room scale, and thin sheets break the first-iteration witness. Our field is also smooth at the scale of σ \sigma . At high flux, a neural surface is therefore sharper where views are dense, and on Transientangelo’s three-view simulated scenes, our depth error is up to 1.36 times theirs above 10 PPP (Sec. S7). There, because our solid fills space that no training view sees, our Chamfer distance is up to 32 times theirs. On two validation scenes, adding ten times as many ambient photons as were recorded raises our error at 0.1 PPP up to tenfold (Sec. S5, which lists other limitations). Future work may refine the grid where views are dense, derive witnesses for thin sheets and estimate camera poses jointly. We also plan to extend the closure to other range sensors.
